questions.evidence: The hole, or cup, is always found within the green and must have a diameter of 108 millimeters (4.25 in) and a depth of at least 10 centimeters (3.94 in).

questions.q: How long did the longest tennis match in history, John Isner against Nicolas Mahut at Wimbledon in 2010, last in total?
questions.fact: It was spread over three days. The final set alone ended 70–68.

source.name: Wikipedia: Isner–Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships

questions.evidence: in 11 hours and 5 minutes over three days. It was the longest tennis match in professional history.

questions.q: What is the lowest natural temperature ever directly recorded on the ground on Earth?
questions.fact: It was measured at Vostok Station in Antarctica in 1983. The same station had already set the record in 1968.

source.name: Wikipedia: Lowest temperature recorded on Earth

questions.evidence: The lowest natural temperature ever directly recorded at ground level on Earth is −89.2 °C (−128.6 °F; 184.0 K) at the then-Soviet Vostok Station in Antarctica on 21 July 1983

questions.q: How old was Mary Shelley when her novel Frankenstein was first published?
questions.fact: It was published anonymously, so many readers assumed her husband, the poet Percy Shelley, had written it.
questions.evidence: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley (née Godwin; 30 August 1797 – 1 February 1851) … Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, published on 1 January 1818

questions.q: How fast did a French TGV train go when it set the world speed record for a train on steel wheels in 2007?
questions.fact: The record run took place on 3 April 2007 on the brand new LGV Est line in eastern France.
questions.evidence: The top speed of 574.8 km/h (159.7 m/s, 357.2 mph) was reached

questions.q: How much does an Oscar statuette weigh?
questions.fact: It is made of gold-plated bronze and shows a knight holding a sword, standing on a reel of film.
questions.evidence: it is 13.5 in (34.3 cm) tall, weighs 8.5 lb (3.9 kg)

questions.q: How long is Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody", as released on the original 1975 single?
questions.fact: It was the UK's Christmas number one in 1975 and stayed at the top for nine weeks.
questions.evidence: Length | 5:55

questions.q: At what temperature does liquid nitrogen boil?
questions.fact: Put it in a vacuum chamber and it can be cooled further until it freezes solid at −210 °C.
questions.evidence: It has a boiling point of about −196 °C (−321 °F; 77 K).

questions.q: How old was Edmund Hillary when he and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit of Mount Everest?
questions.fact: He and Tenzing Norgay were the first climbers confirmed to have reached the top, on 29 May 1953.
questions.evidence: Sir Edmund Percival Hillary (20 July 1919 – 11 January 2008) … On 29 May 1953, he and Tenzing Norgay became the first climbers confirmed to have reached the summit of Mount Everest.

questions.q: What is the top speed of Formula Rossa, the record-breaking roller coaster at Ferrari World in Abu Dhabi?
questions.fact: Riders reach top speed just 4.9 seconds after launch.
questions.evidence: became the fastest roller coaster in the world upon opening with a maximum speed of 240 km/h (149.1 mph)

questions.q: How much does the Tsar Bell in Moscow's Kremlin weigh?
questions.fact: It is the largest bell in the world. It cracked in a fire soon after it was made and has never been rung.
questions.evidence: The bell is the largest bell in the world, weighing 201,924 kilograms (445,166 lb)

questions.q: What is the theatrical running time of The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (2003)?
questions.fact: It won all 11 Academy Awards it was nominated for, including Best Picture. That ties the record held by Ben-Hur and Titanic.

source.name: Wikipedia: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King

questions.evidence: Running time | 201 minutes

questions.q: What is the average surface temperature on Venus?
questions.fact: Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System. The air pressure at its surface is 92 times Earth's.
questions.evidence: the average surface temperature is 737 K (464 °C; 867 °F)

questions.q: How old was Steve Jobs when he co-founded Apple?
questions.fact: Apple started out in Jobs's bedroom at his parents' house before moving into the garage.
questions.evidence: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) … as a business partnership in Jobs's parents' Crist Drive home on April 1, 1976.

questions.q: What is the fastest recorded delivery in international cricket, bowled by Pakistan's Shoaib Akhtar?
questions.fact: His nickname was the "Rawalpindi Express".
questions.evidence: He achieved the record of the fastest recorded bowl to date at 161.3 km/h

questions.q: How long is an official marathon race?
questions.fact: The name comes from the legend of Pheidippides, a Greek messenger. The distance was only standardised in 1921.
questions.evidence: The marathon is a long-distance foot race with a distance of 42.195 kilometres (c. 26.22 mi)

questions.q: What is Usain Bolt's 100 metres world record time, set in 2009?
questions.fact: It was the biggest improvement in the record since electronic timing began.
questions.evidence: Bolt improved upon his second 100 m world record of 9.69 with 9.58 seconds in 2009

questions.q: How tall was Robert Wadlow, the tallest person in recorded history?
questions.fact: He kept growing all his adult life, because of an overactive pituitary gland. He died aged 22.
questions.evidence: Robert Pershing Wadlow (February 22, 1918 – July 15, 1940) … was an American man known for being the tallest person in recorded history for whom there is irrefutable evidence. … Wadlow's height was 8 ft 11.1 in (2.72 m)

questions.q: What is the population of Europe?
questions.fact: Europe's population grew from about 100 million in 1700 to 400 million by 1900.
questions.evidence: The population of Europe was about 742 million in 2023 according to UN estimates.

questions.q: Counting from Robert Walpole in 1721, how many people have been British prime minister, up to and including Andy Burnham?
questions.fact: Walpole is still the longest-serving prime minister: he led the government for over twenty years.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of prime ministers of the United Kingdom

questions.evidence: The list runs from Robert Walpole (1st) to Keir Starmer (58th) and Andy Burnham (59th), each person counted once however many terms they served. Prime Minister of the United Kingdom: "The current prime minister is Andy Burnham who has held the office since 20 July 2026."

questions.q: How old was Jeanne Calment, the oldest person ever, when she died?
questions.fact: She lived in Arles, and claimed to remember selling coloured pencils to Vincent van Gogh.
questions.evidence: Jeanne Louise Calment (21 February 1875 – 4 August 1997) was a French supercentenarian who is the oldest person in recorded history whose age has been verified, with a documented lifespan of 122 years and 164 days.

questions.q: How old was Sweden's Oscar Swahn when he became the oldest person ever to win an Olympic gold medal?
questions.fact: He won it for shooting at moving deer targets. Eight years later, aged 72, he won a silver too.
questions.evidence: At 64 years and 258 days of age, he became the oldest gold medalist ever, a record he still holds. … At the 1920 Summer Olympics, he became the oldest athlete ever to compete in the Olympics at the age of 72.

questions.q: What is the population of Egypt?
questions.fact: It is the most populous country in the Arab world, and the third most populous in Africa.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of countries by population (United Nations)

questions.evidence: Egypt: Population (1 July 2023) 114,535,772 (UN World Population Prospects, 2024 revision)

questions.q: What is the population of Saudi Arabia?
questions.fact: Oil was discovered there in 1938. It is now the world's second-largest oil producer.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of countries by population (United Nations)

questions.evidence: Saudi Arabia: Population (1 July 2023) 32,264,292 (UN World Population Prospects, 2024 revision)

questions.q: What is the population of Iran?
questions.fact: Iran was known for centuries as Persia. Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Empire there in the 6th century BC.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of countries by population (United Nations)

questions.evidence: Iran: Population (1 July 2023) 90,608,707 (UN World Population Prospects, 2024 revision)

questions.q: What is the population of Russia?
questions.fact: It is the largest country in the world, spanning eleven time zones.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of countries by population (United Nations)

questions.evidence: Russia: Population (1 July 2023) 145,440,500 (UN World Population Prospects, 2024 revision)

questions.q: What is the population of Brazil?
questions.fact: It is the only Portuguese-speaking country in the Americas, and has more Portuguese speakers than any other country.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of countries by population (United Nations)

questions.evidence: Brazil: Population (1 July 2023) 211,140,729 (UN World Population Prospects, 2024 revision)

questions.q: What is the population of Turkey?
questions.fact: Istanbul is its largest city, but the capital is Ankara.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of countries by population (United Nations)

questions.evidence: Turkey: Population (1 July 2023) 87,270,501 (UN World Population Prospects, 2024 revision)

questions.q: What is the population of Vietnam?
questions.fact: Its capital is Hanoi, but its largest city is Ho Chi Minh City.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of countries by population (United Nations)

questions.evidence: Vietnam: Population (1 July 2023) 100,352,192 (UN World Population Prospects, 2024 revision)

questions.q: What is the population of Pakistan?
questions.fact: Its largest city is Karachi; the capital is Islamabad.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of countries by population (United Nations)

questions.evidence: Pakistan: Population (1 July 2023) 247,504,495 (UN World Population Prospects, 2024 revision)

questions.q: How many sheets of A4 paper would it take to cover a football (soccer) pitch?
questions.fact: An A0 sheet is exactly one square metre, and each size down is half the one before, so A4 is a sixteenth of a square metre.
questions.evidence: FIFA recommends that the field of play measures exactly 105 metres (115 yards) long and 68 metres (74 yards) wide … Paper size: A4 is 297 mm by 210 mm. 7,140 m2 / (0.297 m x 0.210 m = 0.06237 m2) = 114,478

questions.q: How far is it from one end of San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge to the other, including the approach spans?
questions.fact: When it opened in 1937, its 1,280 m main span was the longest of any suspension bridge in the world, a record it held until 1964.
questions.evidence: The total length of the Golden Gate Bridge from abutment to abutment is 8,981 feet (2,737 m).

questions.q: How far do trains travel through the Channel Tunnel, from its entrance in England to its exit in France?
questions.fact: Its 37.9 km undersea section is the longest underwater stretch of any tunnel in the world.
questions.evidence: The Channel Tunnel is a 50.46-kilometre railway tunnel beneath the English Channel which connects Folkestone in the United Kingdom with Coquelles

questions.q: How far is it from the southern tip of Manhattan island to its northern tip?
questions.fact: It is only about 3.7 km (2.3 miles) wide at 14th Street.
questions.evidence: The island is about 13.4 miles (21.6 km) from north to south

questions.q: On average, how far is the Moon from the Earth?
questions.fact: Its orbit isn't a perfect circle: it swings between roughly 363,000 km and 405,000 km from Earth.
questions.evidence: The mean distance of the Moon from the Earth is 384401 km. (Infobox semi-major axis 384,399 km; periapsis 362,600 km, apoapsis 405,400 km.)

questions.q: How far did the riders race in total over the 21 stages of the 2025 Tour de France?
questions.fact: Tadej Pogačar won it, his fourth Tour de France victory.
questions.evidence: Distance 3,301.9 km (2,051.7 mi)

questions.q: How high above the equator do geostationary satellites, such as TV satellites, orbit?
questions.fact: At that height a satellite circles once a day, keeping pace with the Earth's spin, so it seems to hang still in the sky.
questions.evidence: a circular geosynchronous orbit 35,786 km (22,236 mi) in altitude above Earth's equator

questions.q: How far was Mars from the Earth at its closest approach in 2003?
questions.fact: That was the nearest Mars had come in almost 60,000 years.
questions.evidence: in 2003 the minimum distance was 55.76 million km, nearer than any such encounter in almost 60,000 years

questions.q: On average, how far is the Earth from the Sun?
questions.fact: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 19 seconds to reach us.
questions.evidence: 1 astronomical unit = 149,597,870.700 kilometres (exactly), approximately the average Earth-Sun distance; sunlight travels for 8 minutes and 19 seconds before reaching Earth

questions.q: How many pints would it take to fill the bowl of London's Wembley Stadium to the brim?
questions.fact: Building it took 90,000 m³ of concrete and 23,000 tonnes of steel.
questions.evidence: The bowl volume is listed at 1,139,100 m3 … The imperial pint is … 568.26125 millilitres. 1,139,100,000 L / 0.56826125 L = 2,004,535,766

questions.q: How many times more heavy is the Sun than the Earth?
questions.fact: The Sun holds about 99.86% of all the mass in the Solar System.
questions.evidence: The Sun's mass is around 330,000 times that of Earth, making up about 99.86% of the total mass of the Solar System.

questions.q: How many 1p coins, stacked one on top of another, would it take to reach the top of London's Shard?
questions.fact: Pennies made since 1992 are copper-plated steel, a little thicker than the old bronze ones (1.65 mm against 1.52 mm).
questions.evidence: Penny thickness: (Steel) 1.65 mm. The Shard: Standing 309.6 metres high. 309.6 m / 0.00165 m = 187,636

questions.q: How many football (soccer) pitches would fit inside New York's Central Park?
questions.fact: It gets an estimated 42 million visits a year, the most of any city park in the United States.
questions.evidence: containing 843 acres (3.41 km2) … FIFA recommends that the field of play measures exactly 105 metres long and 68 metres wide. 843 acres = 3,411,500 m2 / 7,140 m2 = 478

questions.q: On average, how many litres of water go over Niagara Falls every second?
questions.fact: In summer at least 2,800 m³ a second goes over, about 90% of it over the Horseshoe Falls.
questions.evidence: The average annual flow rate is 2,400 m3/s. (1 m3 = 1,000 litres, so 2,400,000 litres a second.)

questions.q: How many Eiffel Towers, stacked on top of each other, would it take to reach the summit of Mount Everest?
questions.fact: The tower grew 6 metres in 2022, when a digital radio antenna was fixed to the top.
questions.evidence: The tower is 330 m tall (since the antenna of 15 March 2022). Everest: the new official height is 8,848.86 m. 8,848.86 / 330 = 26.8

questions.q: How many Wembley Stadiums could you fill with the water in Scotland's Loch Ness?
questions.fact: Loch Ness holds more water than all the lakes in England and Wales put together.
questions.evidence: Loch Ness volume 1.8 cu mi (7.5 km3). Wembley: the bowl volume is listed at 1,139,100 m3. 7.50 billion m3 / 1,139,100 m3 = 6,587
